module purpose: neorv32_debug_dm decodes debugger DMI requests, optionally qualified by an authenticator sub-unit, into writes of debug control registers (dmcontrol halt/resume/reset-acknowledge/hart-select/ndmreset/dmactive, abstract command, abstractauto, program buffer, data0); it runs an abstract-command state machine that checks the command, builds a load/store instruction and triggers execution on the selected hart, tracks per-hart halted/resume/reset status from CPU bus writes, serves CPU bus reads of the code ROM, instruction image, data register and request flags, returns status on DMI reads, and drives halt_req_o and ndmrstn_o.

use-case flows.value: DMI request decode: write/read decision from the request op, qualified by the authentication result
authentication result that blocks DMI register writes, status readback, the halt request and the ndmreset output when the authenticator is built in
dmcontrol fields: halt request, resume request, reset acknowledge, hart select and ndmreset on an authorized write; dmactive on any DMI write
abstractauto auto-execute enables for data0 and the two program buffer words
program buffer words written by the debugger
abstract command written and started, directly or by auto-execute on a data0/progbuf access
abstract-command execution: command check, load/store instruction generation, execute request to the selected hart, wait for acknowledgements; instruction image presented to the CPU
busy and pending-error state that block writes of command, abstractauto, program buffer and data0 while a command runs or an error is pending
command error code from illegal command, illegal hart state, CPU exception and busy-access errors, cleared on request
halt request to the selected hart and non-debug-module reset to the system
per-hart halted, resume-request, resume-acknowledge and reset status updated from CPU acknowledgements and DMI requests
data0 register exchanged between the debugger (DMI) and the CPU (bus)
CPU bus access decode: debug-mode strobe qualified read and full-word write
DMI readback of dmstatus, dmcontrol, abstractcs, abstractauto, data0, authdata and haltsum0; CPU bus readback of code ROM, instruction image, data0 and request flags
control registers forced to constants while rstn_i is low; command controller cleared while dmactive is 0; hart status cleared while ndmreset is 1

conceptual assets.concept: Debugger access authorization -- whether a DMI write or read is allowed to take effect, and the authentication exchange that decides it
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dmi_wren_auth <= dmi_wren when (not AUTHENTICATOR) or (auth.valid = '1') else '0';` (line 212) and the read twin at line 213 qualify every protected write (lines 425, 438, 443, 453, 459, 464, 469, 495) and the read-side error and auto-execute decisions (lines 626, 635); auth.valid also gates halt_req_o (line 500), ndmrstn_o (line 505) and DMI status readback (lines 530, 555, 604). Integrity: each authorized decision must equal the op decode AND the authentication result. Availability: the decision is produced in the cycle the request op and auth.valid hold. auth.valid enters this entity from neorv32_debug_auth_inst.valid_o (CONNECTS, occurrence 14, line 745) in AUTHENTICATOR builds and is constant '1' otherwise (line 754); it is tested in when/if conditions (lines 212, 530), so the sub-unit wiring exception holds, and it 'sets' the decision without any inference about the authenticator's internals. dmi_wren_auth and dmi_rden_auth compute the authorized decisions (GATED_BY auth.valid, occurrence 2). dmi_wren computes the write decode (GATED_BY dmi_req_i.op, line 209) and is itself the only qualifier of the dmactive write (line 432) and of the authenticator write strobe (line 748). auth.we and auth.re (lines 747-748, AUTHENTICATOR builds only) are computed here from dmi_wren/dmi_rden and the authdata address and delivered to the unsupplied authenticator (connections we_i/re_i, lines 738-739) together with wdata_i (line 740): the integrity of the strobes it receives is Established by the delivering lines. Not listed: dmi_rden is an operand of dmi_rden_auth and auth.re and otherwise only acknowledges (line 524); dmi_req_i and dmi_rsp_o are complete DMI transaction records (address, op, write data / read data, ack) and are excluded as transport; auth.rdata and auth.busy only receive sub-unit outputs and are read as data (lines 549-550, 610), so they are carriers. Confidentiality is not selected: the readback gate exists only when the AUTHENTICATOR generic is true, which is chosen outside this RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: Debug module active state -- the enable of the abstract-command controller and qualifier of the halt and ndmreset outputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_reg.dmcontrol_dmactive <= dmi_req_i.data(0);` (line 433) is written under `if (dmi_wren = '1')` (line 432), the only dmcontrol field not qualified by dmi_wren_auth. While it is 0 the controller is forced to CMD_IDLE and ldsw_progbuf, req_exe, pbuf_en, illegal flags and cmderr are cleared (lines 229-236, GATES records at occurrence 2); it is an operand of halt_req_o (line 500) and ndmrstn_o (line 505) and is wired to the authenticator enable_i (line 743). Integrity: controller state transitions and both outputs follow the stored value. Availability: held between writes, reset to 0 by rstn_i (line 399). It stores the state (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 433). Its readback through dmi_rsp_o.data (line 569) is a transport field, not an exit.

conceptual assets.concept: Non-debug-module reset request -- the system reset the debugger asserts through the module
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_reg.dmcontrol_ndmreset <= dmi_req_i.data(1);` (line 430) on an authorized dmcontrol write (lines 424-425) is held and drives `ndmrstn_o <= '0' when (dm_reg.dmcontrol_ndmreset = '1') and (dm_reg.dmcontrol_dmactive = '1') and ((not AUTHENTICATOR) or (auth.valid = '1')) else '1';` (line 505); it also clears hart halted/resume status and sets hart_reset (lines 355-383). Integrity: the reset output must be asserted exactly under these conditions and the hart status must follow it. Availability: the request is held between writes and delivered combinationally on ndmrstn_o. dm_reg.dmcontrol_ndmreset stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 7; GATES ndmrstn_o at occurrence 8); ndmrstn_o is the exit port (GATED_BY dm_reg.dmcontrol_ndmreset, occurrence 2), whose consumer lies outside the supplied RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: Hart halt request -- the request that stops the selected hart and enters debug mode
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_reg.halt_req <= dmi_req_i.data(31);` (line 426) on an authorized dmcontrol write is held and drives `halt_req_o(i) <= dm_reg.halt_req and dm_reg.hartsel_dec(i) and dm_reg.dmcontrol_dmactive when ((not AUTHENTICATOR) or (auth.valid = '1')) else '0';` (line 500). Integrity: the per-hart request must equal this conjunction. Availability: held between writes and driven continuously. dm_reg.halt_req stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3; SOURCES halt_req_o at occurrence 4); halt_req_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM dm_reg.halt_req, occurrence 2), delivering to harts outside the supplied RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: Hart selection -- which hart the halt, resume, reset-acknowledge and execute requests address, and whether the selection is valid
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_reg.hartsel <= dmi_req_i.data(18 downto 16);` (line 429) is held and decoded by `dm_reg.hartsel_dec(i) <= '1' when (dm_reg.hartsel(2) = '0') and (dm_reg.hartsel(1 downto 0) = ...) else '0';` (line 487). hartsel_dec routes the halt request (line 500), resume request (line 366), reset acknowledge (line 384) and execute request (line 298), and qualifies the command hart-state check (line 266) and status (lines 534-545). `dm_reg.hartsel_inv <= '0' when (unsigned(dm_reg.hartsel) < NUM_HARTS) else '1';` (line 489) computes the invalid-selection status reported at lines 538-539. Integrity: requests and status must address exactly the encoded hart. hartsel stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3; GATES dm_reg.hartsel_dec); hartsel_dec computes the decoded selection (GATED_BY dm_reg.hartsel, occurrence 9); hartsel_inv computes the validity result (GATED_BY dm_reg.hartsel, occurrence 2). dci.req_exe copies hartsel_dec only in CMD_TRIGGER and is listed under the execute handshake.

conceptual assets.concept: Hart resume handshake -- the pending resume request per hart and its acknowledgement
conceptual assets.reasoning: A resume pulse `dm_reg.req_res <= dmi_req_i.data(30);` (line 427, cleared each cycle at line 417) sets `dm_ctrl.hart_resume_req(i) <= '1'` for the selected hart (lines 366-367), which is cleared by the CPU acknowledgement dci.ack_res (line 369) or ndmreset (line 365). dci.ack_res is captured from a CPU bus write to the status-register area (lines 676-680) and sets hart_resume_ack (line 376) and clears hart_halted (line 360); hart_resume_ack is reported in dmstatus (lines 536-537). Integrity: the request presented to the hart and the reported acknowledgement must follow these set/clear rules. Availability: the request is held until acknowledged. Roles: req_res stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 6; GATES hart_resume_req); hart_resume_req stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 4): the map records only SOURCES dci.req_res, but the RTL `dci.req_res(i) <= dm_ctrl.hart_resume_req(i);` (line 501, all indices) is a plain copy that is read into bus_rsp_o.data (line 699), so the register's value is what the hart reads and dci.req_res is not listed separately; dci.ack_res stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 7; GATES hart state); hart_resume_ack stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 4; SOURCES dmi_rsp_o.data).

conceptual assets.concept: Hart reset status -- whether a hart has been reset by ndmreset and not yet acknowledged
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_ctrl.hart_reset(i) <= '1'` while ndmreset is set (line 383) and is cleared by `elsif (dm_reg.reset_ack = '1') and (dm_reg.hartsel_dec(i) = '1')` (lines 384-385), where reset_ack is a pulse written from dmi_req_i.data(28) on an authorized dmcontrol write (line 428, cleared at line 418). The status is reported in dmstatus (lines 534-535). Integrity: the reported reset state must follow these rules. dm_ctrl.hart_reset stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 3; SOURCES dmi_rsp_o.data); dm_reg.reset_ack stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 5; GATES dm_ctrl.hart_reset).

conceptual assets.concept: Hart halted status -- whether each hart is halted in debug mode, which gates abstract-command execution
conceptual assets.reasoning: dci.ack_hlt is captured from a CPU bus write to the status-register area (lines 676-679) and sets `dm_ctrl.hart_halted(i) <= '1'` (line 358); ack_res clears it (line 360) and ndmreset clears it (line 356). The command check admits a command only if `or_reduce_f(dm_ctrl.hart_halted and dm_reg.hartsel_dec) = '1'` (line 266), otherwise illegal_state is raised (line 269); ack_hlt also ends CMD_BUSY (line 305). The status is reported in dmstatus and haltsum0 (lines 542-545, 615). Integrity: command execution and reports must follow the actual halt acknowledgements. dm_ctrl.hart_halted stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 5; GATES dm_ctrl.state); dci.ack_hlt stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 6; GATES dm_ctrl.state). cpu_rsp_dec, which picks the acknowledging hart, is constant all-ones in the default single-hart build (line 715) and only routes the acknowledgement in multi-hart builds (line 723), so it is not listed.

conceptual assets.concept: Abstract command -- the debugger command that selects the register transfer the hart executes
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_reg.command <= dmi_req_i.data;` (line 439) is accepted only when `(dmi_req_i.addr = addr_command_c) and (dmi_wren_auth = '1') and (dm_ctrl.busy = '0') and (dm_ctrl.cmderr = 000)` (line 438). Its fields decide command legality (lines 261-265), whether a load or store is generated and the register number inserted (lines 279-288), and whether the program buffer runs (line 293). Integrity: the generated instruction and the legality decision must follow the stored command. Availability: held between accepted writes. It stores the command (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 14; GATES dm_ctrl.state and dm_ctrl.ldsw_progbuf).

conceptual assets.concept: Abstract-command controller state -- the sequencing of check, prepare, trigger, busy and error phases
conceptual assets.reasoning: `case dm_ctrl.state is` (line 245) sequences CMD_IDLE to CMD_CHECK on a command write or auto-execute (lines 249-256), to CMD_PREPARE or CMD_ERROR after the legality and halted checks (lines 261-274), to CMD_TRIGGER (line 294), to CMD_BUSY on execute acknowledge (lines 299-300) and back to CMD_IDLE on halt acknowledge (lines 305-306). Each phase selects which outputs are produced (SELECTS dci.req_exe, dm_ctrl.ldsw_progbuf, dm_ctrl.pbuf_en, illegal flags at occurrence 4). Integrity: execute requests and instruction generation happen only in the implemented order. Availability: under dmactive the controller returns to CMD_IDLE from CMD_ERROR and others (lines 311, 315). It stores the state (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 5, line 252).

conceptual assets.concept: Command busy lock -- the decision that a command is in progress, which freezes command, abstractauto, program buffer and data0
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_ctrl.busy <= '0' when (dm_ctrl.state = CMD_IDLE) else '1';` (line 339) blocks writes of command (line 438), abstractauto (line 443), progbuf (lines 464, 469) and data0 (line 495) while a command runs, and turns such writes and data/progbuf reads into access errors (lines 474-478, 626-628); it is reported in abstractcs (line 587). Integrity: the lock must hold exactly while the controller is not idle, so the program and data the hart is using cannot change underneath it. It computes the decision (GATED_BY dm_ctrl.state, occurrence 2).

conceptual assets.concept: Execute handshake -- the request that makes the selected hart run the instruction image, and its acknowledgement
conceptual assets.reasoning: In CMD_TRIGGER `dci.req_exe <= dm_reg.hartsel_dec;` (line 298), cleared every other cycle (line 240) and while dmactive is 0 (line 232); the hart reads it through `bus_rsp_o.data(i*8+1) <= dci.req_exe(i);` (line 700). dci.ack_exe is captured from a CPU bus write (lines 676, 681) and moves the controller to CMD_BUSY (lines 299-300). Integrity: only the selected hart is requested, only in the trigger phase, and the controller advances only on its acknowledgement. dci.req_exe stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 5; SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data, an output field); dci.ack_exe stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 5; GATES dm_ctrl.state).

conceptual assets.concept: Command error status -- the error code of the last abstract command and the error events that set or clear it
conceptual assets.reasoning: While no error is pending, cmderr is set by illegal_state (line 322), the CPU exception report dci.ack_exc (line 324), illegal_cmd (line 326) or a busy access error (lines 327-328), and is cleared only by clr_acc_err (lines 330-331). A pending error blocks new command writes (line 438) and command start (line 251), and is reported in abstractcs (line 589). illegal_state and illegal_cmd are the hart-state and legality decisions of CMD_CHECK (lines 269, 273); dci.ack_exc is captured from a CPU bus write (line 682); wr_acc_err and rd_acc_err are raised by accesses while busy (lines 478, 628); clr_acc_err by an authorized abstractcs write with bits 10-8 set (lines 459-460). Integrity: the error code and the lock it imposes must follow these events. Each is a register: cmderr stores (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 6; GATES dm_reg.command), and each error flag stores its decision (CLOCKED_BY at the cited occurrence; GATES dm_ctrl.cmderr).

conceptual assets.concept: Debug instruction image -- the program buffer and generated load/store instruction the hart fetches and executes in debug mode
conceptual assets.reasoning: The debugger writes `dm_reg.progbuf(0) <= dmi_req_i.data;` (line 465, and line 470 for word 1) when not busy. In CMD_PREPARE the controller builds `dm_ctrl.ldsw_progbuf` from instr_sw_c/instr_lw_c, the data address and dm_reg.command(4 downto 0) (lines 279-291) and sets `dm_ctrl.pbuf_en <= dm_reg.command(18);` (line 293). The image is `cpu_progbuf(0) <= dm_ctrl.ldsw_progbuf;`, `cpu_progbuf(1) <= instr_nop_c when (dm_ctrl.pbuf_en = '0') else dm_reg.progbuf(0);`, the same for word 2, and `cpu_progbuf(3) <= instr_ebreak_c;` (lines 508-511), returned to the CPU fetch by `bus_rsp_o.data <= cpu_progbuf(...)` (line 694). Integrity: the instructions the hart executes must be exactly the stored program words and the generated transfer instruction. progbuf stores a configure-flow setting read by the cpu_progbuf selection (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 3; SOURCES cpu_progbuf); pbuf_en stores the decision whether the program buffer runs (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 4; GATES cpu_progbuf); ldsw_progbuf computes the transfer instruction (DERIVES_FROM dm_reg.command, occurrence 6, line 283); its register only feeds cpu_progbuf, so it is listed as computes. cpu_progbuf computes the image (DERIVES_FROM dm_reg.progbuf, occurrence 3): word 0 copies ldsw_progbuf, but words 1-2 are selections and word 3 a constant, so it is not only a copy.

conceptual assets.concept: Debug data register (data0) -- the value exchanged between debugger and hart by abstract register transfers
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dci.data_reg <= dmi_req_i.data;` when `dci.data_reg_we = '1'` (lines 665-666), where data_reg_we requires an authorized, non-busy data0 write (line 495), else `dci.data_reg <= bus_req_i.data;` on a CPU write to the data area (lines 667-668). It is returned to the debugger (line 605, gated by auth.valid at line 604) and to the CPU (line 696). Integrity: the value each side reads must be the last write the arbitration admitted. Availability: held between writes. dci.data_reg stores it (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 4; CARRIES dmi_rsp_o.data and bus_rsp_o.data). dci.data_reg_we only gates the store and is not listed. Confidentiality is not selected: the DMI readback gate depends on the AUTHENTICATOR generic chosen outside this RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: CPU debug-memory access eligibility -- whether a CPU bus access is a debug-mode read or a full-word write that this module serves
conceptual assets.reasoning: `accen <= bus_req_i.debug and bus_req_i.stb;` (line 708), `rden <= accen and (not bus_req_i.rw);` (line 709) and `wren <= accen and (bus_req_i.rw) and and_reduce_f(bus_req_i.ben);` (line 710). wren decides whether a CPU write lands in data0 (line 667) or in the halt/resume/execute/exception acknowledgements (line 676); rden decides whether the code ROM, instruction image, data0 or request flags are returned (line 689). Integrity: these decisions must obey the debug-mode, strobe, direction and byte-enable predicates. wren computes (GATED_BY accen, occurrence 4); rden computes (GATED_BY accen, occurrence 3). accen is an operand of both decisions and otherwise only acknowledges (line 661), so it is not listed; bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o are transaction records and are excluded as transport.

conceptual assets.concept: Auto-execute configuration and triggers -- the enables and access events that restart the abstract command without a command write
conceptual assets.reasoning: `dm_reg.abstractauto_autoexecdata <= dmi_req_i.data(0);` and the two autoexecprogbuf bits (lines 443-446) are written on an authorized, non-busy abstractauto write. They qualify `dm_reg.autoexec_wr <= '1'` on an authorized data0/progbuf write (lines 450-454) and `dm_reg.autoexec_rd <= '1'` on an authorized data0/progbuf read (lines 635-639), and either trigger moves the idle controller to CMD_CHECK (lines 255-256). Integrity: a command restarts only on accesses that the stored enables select. abstractauto_autoexecdata and abstractauto_autoexecprogbuf store the setting (CLOCKED_BY, occurrence 3; GATES dm_reg.autoexec_wr); autoexec_wr and autoexec_rd store the trigger decision (CLOCKED_BY at occurrences 5 and 4; GATES dm_ctrl.state).
